clue.text: Two fellows meet a pedlar

parts.note: a fellow is a chap, the first of the pair
a fellow is a man, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A couple of men encounter a travelling salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapman was an itinerant dealer hawking small goods from door to door, the old word for a hawker.

clue.text: Planting, we hear — and yielding, we see

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the sound of the planting word gives the letters

parts.note: sowing a field is seeding it

explanation.surface: A gardener notes what is heard and seen in the planting season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we see' is only there to balance 'we hear': the written form is the yielding sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceding territory or ground is giving it up, surrendering to another.

clue.text: Weapon, for example, used in inconclusive attack

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the shortened attack word
an attack that is not concluded loses its final letter

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: A weapon is used in a half-hearted assault.
explanation.walkthrough: An assegai is a southern African spear; 'inconclusive' means the attack word stops short of its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples.

clue.text: Messes with partnership at meeting, as result of excessive effort

parts.note: to muck things up is to mess them, so messes gives mucks
we, the two of us, is a partnership
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mess of a joint meeting by trying too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A muck sweat is a heavy, drenching sweat brought on by strenuous exertion or anxiety.

clue.text: Maintain game position — don't mention pass

parts.note: to never say something is not to mention it
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: A card player is told to keep their place and not announce a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means plucky here, not a sport, and 'pass' is death, not a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses a refusal to give up, keeping a plucky stance however bad things look.

clue.text: For example, plane's maximum height

parts.note: the plane is a tree, not an aircraft, so its greatest height is its uppermost branches

explanation.surface: An aircraft's ceiling is being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of any tree, such as a plane, is its crown of top branches.

clue.text: Jack is a formidable person? Not half!

indicators.note: only half of the word for the formidable person is kept, the other half dropped

parts.note: a tartar is a fierce or formidable person

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Jack is a terror, and the reply is a hearty yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' reads as British slang for 'very much so', but here it halves TARTAR. Jack is an old name for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar and tar are both old nicknames for a sailor.

clue.text: Former article, writing in the papers

parts.note: EX means former, as in an ex-partner
a is the indefinite article
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An old item of writing appears in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Examination question sheets are called papers, so sitting papers means taking tests.

clue.text: Capital needed to activate oil distribution

parts.note: to trip a switch is to activate it

indicators.note: distributing the letters of oil scatters them into a new order

explanation.surface: A capital city must start up its oil supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed to' is only a link; Tripoli is also a Lebanese city, but either way it fits 'Capital' as Libya's.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Snatching courage with a mixed gin

parts.note: pluck is courage or nerve

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of gin are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets Dutch courage from a gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucking something is pulling or grabbing it away quickly.

clue.text: Clean cloak that's worn by Jane Eyre, for one

definitions.text: that's worn by Jane Eyre, for one

parts.note: to dust is to clean
to cloak is to cover

explanation.surface: The governess Jane Eyre wears a tidy cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Eyre is the novel, not the heroine, and what a book wears is its jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's paper jacket protecting the binding is what a novel like this wears.

clue.text: Gold can restrict decline for so long

indicators.note: the gold symbol holds the decline word inside it, restricting it

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to die away is to decline

explanation.surface: Gold may limit falling prices for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for so long' is the jaunty farewell, like 'so long'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French farewell, meaning goodbye, just as so long does.

clue.text: A spicy concoction for the old emperor

explanation.surface: A hot drink is offered to a former ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is hot spiced wine and water, and also the title of the former emperors of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Basis for an underground shooting

explanation.surface: Grounds for a shooting in the subway are discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground shooting' is a stem growing under the soil, not gunfire on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Rootstock is a source or origin, and also a rhizome, a stem that grows underground and sends up shoots.

clue.text: Homer's forte?

parts.note: the Homer is a homing pigeon, not the Greek poet, and its strength is finding its way home

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the Greek poet was best at.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of direction, the ability to find one's bearings, is the pigeon's special skill.

clue.text: Progressive measures to raise in a bill, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Reformers plan to put progressive steps in a parliamentary bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeing up of laws or markets is the work of progressive reforms.

clue.text: Check air, with this, a new tree outside city

indicators.note: the rearranged tree letters sit outside the city, enclosing it
new means the letters of tree are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: A newly planted tree outside town is used to test the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TREE into ETER, which goes 'outside' ROME: E-ROME-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument measures the density or weight of gases, so testing air is its use.

clue.text: Cricket can do this using half the Oval, I assume

indicators.note: half of the word Oval is its first two letters

parts.note: to posit something is to assume it as fact

explanation.surface: Someone supposes a cricket match uses only part of the famous London ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, but the cricket is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects lay eggs, often through an ovipositor, and a female cricket does exactly that.

clue.text: An invalid, a true invalid

indicators.note: the second invalid is read as not valid, so the preceding letters are put in a new, valid order

explanation.surface: Someone insists a person is genuinely sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AN INVALID A TRUE describes itself: the whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A valetudinarian is a sickly person, or one anxiously preoccupied with their own health.

clue.text: Where to find sheltered accommodation for drifters

definitions.text: Where to find sheltered accommodation for drifters

parts.words: Where to find sheltered accommodation for drifters
parts.note: the drifters are boats, and the side away from the wind is where they drift and shelter

explanation.surface: A social worker asks where homeless people can find a hostel.
explanation.definitionFit: The downwind side, sheltered from the wind, is the way drifting vessels move.

clue.text: Opened up salt fish

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Salted fish is opened up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask that is broached has been pierced, so its contents are open and flowing.

clue.text: It's old-fashioned to quarrel over a bit of money

indicators.note: in a down clue the quarrel word sits over, above, the rest

parts.note: a feud is a long-running quarrel
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra, a sum of money

explanation.surface: Arguing about small change is a dated habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to medieval lords and vassals, the term describes something outdated.

clue.text: Sensible things no people put in rubbish heap

indicators.note: the no-people pieces go inside the rearranged heap letters
rubbish means the letters of heap are junk to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
men are people

explanation.surface: Wise objects are found, but nobody is put on the rubbish heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' turns HEAP into PHEA, and 'put in' places NOMEN inside: PHE-NOMEN-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are things perceived by the senses, hence sensible in the old meaning.

clue.text: Best barbeque?

parts.note: read as a party held in the open air, a do outside, while also meaning to beat

explanation.surface: Someone asks which grill party is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or surpass someone is to go one better, and an open-air party is an out-door event.

clue.text: Come up with no opening to get together

indicators.note: the opening letter of the come-up word is dropped

parts.note: to emerge is to come up

explanation.surface: Without an opener, people manage to assemble.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite or combine is to come together.

clue.text: Quick to bring back a passenger service

indicators.note: bringing back the service word means reading it in the other direction

parts.note: trams carry passengers through city streets

explanation.surface: A fast way to reinstate public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means brisk or fast, as in a smart pace.

clue.text: Exhaust, say, orchestra, in the bit around the middle

indicators.note: say means the word for exhaust is spoken to give its twin

parts.note: to exhaust resources is to waste them
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Exhaust fumes from an orchestra are in the middle section.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of fabric encircling the trousers or skirt at the midriff.

clue.text: Burden borne by two editors

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Two editors share a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borne by' signals the letters inside 'tWO Editors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is grief or misfortune, something heavy to carry.

clue.text: Unusual to plead for character of Disraeli

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of to plead are set out in a different way

explanation.surface: It is strange to beg on behalf of the Victorian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli was a novelist as well as Prime Minister: Tadpole is a political schemer in his novel Coningsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Tadpole is a party hack in Disraeli's novel Coningsby, alongside his crony Taper.

clue.text: At sea, warn Henry, there's a tusked creature

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of warn are jumbled

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry

explanation.surface: A sailor warns Henry about a tusked sea animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale whose male has a long spiral tusk.
